outcome: Adverse pregnancy outcome (birthweight <3rd centile, pH <=7.10, neonatal intensive care unit admission)
Placental dysfunction (macroscopic/microscopic placental structure abnormalities, placental endocrine dysfunction)
cohort: Women reporting increased fetal movements (IFMs) after 28 weeks' gestation, recruited from two hospitals in the UK.
finding: This prospective study did not find evidence of an association between increased fetal movements (IFM) and adverse pregnancy outcome, nor did it find evidence of underlying placental dysfunction, cord anomalies, intrauterine hypoxia, or infection in pregnancies with IFM.
mod_finding: Women with increased fetal movements (IFM) had similar modes of birth compared to women without IFM in the participating maternity units.
